name: Employees Provident Fund
authority: Employees Provident Fund Act 1991, s.43 and the Third Schedule — Part A (Malaysian citizens, permanent residents and pre-1-August-1998 electors below the age of 60) and Part E (Malaysian citizens aged 60 and above). The first printed row of both Parts is NIL: wages of RM0.01 to RM10.00 attract no contribution, which is the zero band below. A non-citizen contributes under Part F instead, which is the separate EPF_NON_CITIZEN scheme below; an employment belongs to exactly one of the EPF schemes, decided by its employment_statutory_facts registration. A permanent resident or pre-1998 elector who has attained 60 contributes under Part C, which is the separate EPF_PR scheme — the 60-and-above ladder here is Part E and by its own terms reaches Malaysian citizens only, which is what the eligibility predicate says. Contribution ceases at the age of 75 (KWSP, Employer Mandatory Contribution, note 1), which is the zero terminal band. NOT APPLIED: Parts A, C, E and F round THE TOTAL contribution up to the next ringgit, whereas the PERCENT bands above RM20,000 round each share separately and can over-collect by up to RM1 per share per month.

name: Employees Provident Fund (permanent residents aged 60 and above)
authority: Employees Provident Fund Act 1991, s.43 and the Third Schedule Part C — a permanent resident, or a non-citizen who elected to contribute before 1 August 1998, who has attained the age of 60: employee 5.5% of wages, employer 6.5% for wages up to RM5,000 a month and 6% above that, and 5.5% / 6% for the months where wages exceed RM20,000. The printed ladder repeats Part A's brackets (RM10 to RM20, RM20 to RM5,000, RM100 to RM20,000) with the contribution taken on the band's upper limit and rounded up to the next ringgit. Contribution ceases at the age of 75 (KWSP, Employer Mandatory Contribution, note 1). NOT APPLIED: the bands below are DERIVED from the printed rates by that rule, not transcribed — kwsp.gov.my refuses every automated fetch of the Third Schedule PDF (HTTP 403 from its WAF), and the rule reproduces all 800 seeded Part A and Part E bands exactly. Same total-versus-share rounding residue as EPF.

name: Employees Provident Fund (non-citizen employees)
authority: Employees Provident Fund Act 1991, First Schedule para 3 read with the Third Schedule Part F — a non-citizen employee and the employer each contribute 2% of the wages, mandatory from October 2025 wages (November 2025 contribution month). Part F is charged on the wage AS IT STANDS: there is no Third Schedule bracketing and no wage ceiling, which is why this scheme declares no BRACKET_STEP and carries a single open-ended percentage band. NOT APPLIED: KWSP's age-75 contribution ceiling is not applied here — Part F itself prints no age limit and the ceiling is a KWSP-wide administrative rule that has not been confirmed against Part F. NOT APPLIED: Part F rounds THE TOTAL to the next ringgit, this band rounds each share.

name: Social Security Organisation (PERKESO)
authority: Employees Social Security Act 1969, s.2(24) and the Third Schedule (Act 4); the Second Category (Employment Injury Scheme only, employer share only) applies to an employee who has attained the age of sixty. The age-60 split in the bands below IS that rule — the legacy profile keyed it off a hand-maintained `socso_contribution_category` fact instead, which is why an employee whose fact was stale was charged the wrong category. Foreign workers have sat in the same First/Second Category structure since the Invalidity Scheme was extended to them on 1 July 2024 (SOCSO Employer Circular No. 2/2024), so the bands carry no nationality dimension. NOT APPLIED: the Second Category also reaches an employee who first entered the PERKESO scheme at the age of 55 or above (PERKESO, Foreign Workers — Important Note). That limb is a fact about registration history, not about current age, so no WAGE_AND_AGE selector can express it; an employment_statutory_facts registration of the kind EIS already uses would carry it.

name: Employment Insurance System
authority: Employment Insurance System Act 2017, s.2 and the Second Schedule; s.16 read with the First Schedule confines the scheme to employees aged 18 to 60. That age window IS the band ladder below: outside it the scheme awards nothing. The remaining coverage rule — citizens and permanent residents only — is a fact about the person, so it is carried by employment_statutory_facts, which the engine honours as REGISTERED / NOT_REGISTERED. NOT APPLIED: an employee aged 57 or above who has no contribution to the scheme before the age of 57 is exempt (Act 800, per PERKESO, Contributions). That too is a fact about contribution history, not about current age, and the same registration status is where it belongs.

name: Monthly Tax Deduction (Potongan Cukai Bulanan)
authority: Income Tax Act 1967, s.107(2); Income Tax (Deduction from Remuneration) Rules 1994. Both MTD scales are seeded: Category 1 for a taxpayer with no dependent spouse and Category 2 for one who carries a spouse with no total income, the latter holding the second RM400 rebate under ITA 1967 s.6D in its band constants. The category and the RM4,000 s.47 spouse relief are both chosen from employees.spouse_status, which is the question both provisions actually ask — NOT from marital_status, which answers a different one and disagrees with it for a quarter of this population. The flat 30% withholding on a non-resident is expressed as an employment-level PCB rate override, so it is applied only where residence evidence exists and bypasses the resident progressive scale and reliefs. A blank residence or foreign nationality alone does not create that override. NOT APPLIED: (a) the RM6,000 disabled-person and RM5,000 disabled-spouse reliefs — there is one PERSONAL_RELIEF slot and no disability input; (b) the zakat rebate, which has no data home. For the seeded Malaysian population the generator asserts that disabled-person and zakat are claimed by nobody, so only the disabled-SPOUSE relief is actually foregone, by one employee. See MY_PCB_RELIEF_CONSTANTS_UNMODELLED and report §4.4-§4.6. MTD Category 3 (married, spouse working) is assessed on the Category 1 schedule: the spouse relief and the s.6D rebate belong to Category 2 alone, so the category turns on whether the spouse has income of their own, not on marital status.

name: Human Resource Development Levy (HRD Corp)
authority: Pembangunan Sumber Manusia Berhad Act 2001, s.14 and the First Schedule, as expanded to all industries from 1 March 2021. Registration is COMPULSORY at 10 or more Malaysian employees and the levy is 1% of monthly wages; at 5 to 9 Malaysian employees registration is OPTIONAL and the 0.5% levy falls due only once the employer has elected to register (HRD Corp, Registered Employers). NOT APPLIED: that election. The 5-to-9 band below is retained because a registered employer is the common case; an employer at that headcount who has NOT registered is carried by an employment_statutory_facts NOT_REGISTERED status on this scheme, which the engine already honours, and is not expressible in a HEADCOUNT selector. NOT APPLIED: the levy is charged on Malaysian employees only (CEL `!isForeigner ? ... : 0`) and the headcount test counts Malaysian employees only — nothing in the model keys a charge on residency, so a foreign employee is counted and levied too.

name: Non-Employment Injury Security Scheme (LINDUNG 24 Jam)
authority: Employees Social Security Act 1969 (Act 4) — Skim Kemalangan Bukan Bencana Kerja (LINDUNG 24 Jam), in operation 1 June 2026. Employee share only, 0.75% of wages in Phase 1 (years 1-2 from 1 June 2026), rising to 1.00% in Phase 2 (years 3-5) and 1.25% in Phase 3 (year 6 onwards). Charged in both the First and the Second Category — the Second Category, previously employer-only, acquires an employee share — on the same wage bands and the same RM6,000 ceiling as SOCSO, so the ladder below carries no age split and the two categories share one column. The amounts are transcribed from PERKESO's own 65-row Act 4 schedule including SKBBK. A six-month grace period from 1 June 2026 runs before penalties. NOT APPLIED: the Phase 2 and Phase 3 rates — each is a change of law on its own date and belongs to a later sealed version, not to this one.

name: Non-Employment Injury Security Scheme (LINDUNG 24 Jam)
authority: Employees Social Security Act 1969 (Act 4) — Skim Kemalangan Bukan Bencana Kerja (LINDUNG 24 Jam). The eligibility predicate below carries the mandatory limb. NOT APPLIED: the local opt-out. It is an opt-out, not an opt-in — a Malaysian employee keeps paying 0.75% by default and stops only by filing a Release of Liability declaration ('TIDAK MENYERTAI') through PERKESO's LINDUNG Faedah portal, the declaration window having run from 13 July to 31 August 2026. A person-by-person election is not expressible in a band predicate; an employment_statutory_facts REGISTERED / NOT_REGISTERED status on this scheme, of the kind EIS already uses, is what would carry it, and until it does a Malaysian employee is charged NOTHING here rather than the 0.75% the default would collect. Rate, bands, ceiling and phases are otherwise as in the version from 1 June 2026. On 8 July 2026 the Cabinet made the employee contribution VOLUNTARY for Malaysian citizens and permanent residents while leaving it mandatory for non-citizens, and PERKESO opened the election on 13 July 2026 through a Notis Perakuan Pelepasan Liabiliti on the LINDUNG Faedah portal, closing 31 August 2026. Voluntary here means opt-OUT: an employee who files no release continues to participate and contributions continue. So the scheme stays levied on everyone and a release is a per-employment NOT_REGISTERED fact, exactly as EPF and EIS express non-participation — excluding citizens from the scheme itself under-collected from every local who never filed.
